title: Ezekiel Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who cried in Ezekiel's ears with a loud voice commanding men to draw near with destroying weapons?
options: An angel
A man clothed with linen
The LORD
Ezekiel himself
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:1 states that he cried in mine ears with a loud voice, saying, Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near...

questions.question: How many men came from the way of the higher gate with slaughter weapons in their hands?
options: Four
Six
Seven
Five
questions.correctAnswer: Six
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 mentions that six men came from the way of the higher gate, each with a slaughter weapon in his hand.

questions.question: What was the man among the six men clothed with?
options: Leather
Wool
Linen
Silk
questions.correctAnswer: Linen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 describes one man among them clothed with linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side.

questions.question: Where did the six men stand after entering?
options: By the bronze altar
In the courtyard
At the city gate
On the roof
questions.correctAnswer: By the bronze altar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 states that they went in and stood beside the brasen (bronze) altar.

questions.question: From what place did the glory of the God of Israel move?
options: From the cherub to the threshold of the house
From the altar to the city gate
From the temple roof to the courtyard
From the north gate to the east gate
questions.correctAnswer: From the cherub to the threshold of the house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:3 says the glory of the God of Israel went up from the cherub to the threshold of the house.

questions.question: Who did the LORD call after the glory of God moved?
options: The man clothed with linen
The six men with weapons
Ezekiel
The priests
questions.correctAnswer: The man clothed with linen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:3 states God called to the man clothed with linen, who had the writer's inkhorn by his side.

questions.question: What was the man clothed with linen commanded to do in the city?
options: Set a mark on the foreheads of men who sighed and cried for abominations
Slay all the people in the city
Build a wall around Jerusalem
Gather the priests together
questions.correctAnswer: Set a mark on the foreheads of men who sighed and cried for abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:4 commands the man clothed with linen to set a mark upon the foreheads of men that sigh and cry for all the abominations done in the city.

questions.question: True or False: The men with destroying weapons were told to spare those with the mark on their foreheads.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 states they should not come near any man upon whom is the mark.

questions.question: True or False: The command was to slay only the old men and women in the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 commands to slay utterly old and young, maids, little children, and women, not only old men and women.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 9, where were the men with slaughter weapons instructed to begin their work?
options: At the ancient men before the house
At the city gate
At the market square
At the temple roof
questions.correctAnswer: At the ancient men before the house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 says they should begin at the ancient men which were before the house.

questions.question: What did the LORD command the men to do to the house and courts after slaying people?
options: Defile the house and fill the courts with the slain
Cleanse the house and courts
Build a new altar
Gather the survivors
questions.correctAnswer: Defile the house and fill the courts with the slain
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:7 records the LORD's command to defile the house and fill the courts with the slain.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel fell upon his face and cried out asking if the LORD would destroy the rest of Israel in His fury.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:8 describes Ezekiel falling upon his face and crying out, asking if the LORD would destroy all the residue of Israel.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give for His fury and recompense upon Israel and Judah?
options: The iniquity of the house is exceeding great and the land is full of blood
They have built many altars
They have worshiped idols only
They have been faithful but weak
questions.correctAnswer: The iniquity of the house is exceeding great and the land is full of blood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 states the iniquity of Israel and Judah is exceeding great and the land is full of blood, the city full of perverseness.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said He would have pity and spare the inhabitants of the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:10 clearly says the LORD's eye shall not spare nor have pity, but will recompense their way upon their head.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 9, which instruction comes first?
options: The men with weapons to smite the people
The man clothed with linen to mark the foreheads
The glory of God moving from the cherub
The command to defile the house
questions.correctAnswer: The men with weapons to smite the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:1 commands those with charge over the city to draw near with destroying weapons, which is the first instruction before marking and other actions.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 9:5, what instruction was given to those who were to follow the man marked in the city?
options: Spare no one and have no pity as they smite through the city
Only warn the people and do not kill anyone
Mark the foreheads of the righteous
Build a sanctuary in the city
questions.correctAnswer: Spare no one and have no pity as they smite through the city
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:5 states that the men were commanded to follow the man with the mark and smite without sparing or pity. This connects to the judgment theme seen in verses 6 and 7, where the slaughter begins.

questions.question: What groups of people were to be slain according to Ezekiel 9:6?
options: Only the ancient men before the house
Old and young, maids, little children, and women
Only the priests and elders
All men but spare the women and children
questions.correctAnswer: Old and young, maids, little children, and women
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 explicitly commands the killing of old and young alike, including maids, little children, and women, indicating comprehensive judgment, except those marked as protected.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 9:6, where were the slayers instructed to begin the execution?
options: At the king's palace
At the ancient men before the house
At the city gates
At the marketplace
questions.correctAnswer: At the ancient men before the house
questions.explanation: The verse 6 instructs that the slaying should begin at God's sanctuary with the ancient men before the house, emphasizing the seriousness of judgment starting from the leaders or elders.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 9:7 describe as the result of the slaying in the city?
options: The city would be filled with the slain and the house defiled
The city would be rebuilt and purified
The people would repent and return to God
The slayers would be blessed and rewarded
questions.correctAnswer: The city would be filled with the slain and the house defiled
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:7 describes that the slayers were to defile the house and fill the courts with the slain, illustrating the extent of destruction and judgment in Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 9:8, how did the prophet Ezekiel respond when he saw the destruction happening?
options: He fell on his face and cried out to the Lord
He joined the slayers in their task
He fled the city in fear
He remained silent and watched
questions.correctAnswer: He fell on his face and cried out to the Lord
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows Ezekiel's emotional response where he falls on his face and prays to God, expressing concern about the destruction of the remnant of Israel in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What reason does God give in Ezekiel 9:9 for the judgment and destruction upon Jerusalem?
options: The iniquity of Israel and Judah was exceeding great, and the land was full of blood and perverseness
The people had forgotten to build the temple
The kings had become wealthy and proud
The neighboring nations had attacked
questions.correctAnswer: The iniquity of Israel and Judah was exceeding great, and the land was full of blood and perverseness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 explains that the great sinfulness and bloodshed in the land, along with the people's perverseness and rejection of God's presence, led to the judgment described.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 9:10, how does God declare He will respond to the iniquity of the people?
options: He will not spare or have pity but will recompense their way upon their head
He will forgive them and restore the city
He will send prophets to warn them
He will remove the judgment if they repent
questions.correctAnswer: He will not spare or have pity but will recompense their way upon their head
questions.explanation: Verse 10 makes clear God's firm stance on judgment without pity, emphasizing that He will repay their wickedness directly and justly.

questions.question: What report does the man clothed with linen give after completing his task, according to Ezekiel 9:11?
options: He reports that he has done as commanded
He asks for forgiveness for the slain
He refuses to carry out the command
He requests guidance for the next task
questions.correctAnswer: He reports that he has done as commanded
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:11 states that the man clothed with linen reports back that he has fulfilled the instructions given by God, demonstrating obedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 9:5, the men were instructed to have pity and spare the innocent in the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:5 clearly states that the men were to smite without sparing or having pity, indicating total judgment on the unmarked.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 9:6 teaches that the men were to avoid harming those who had the mark on their foreheads.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 6 instructs the slayers not to come near any man upon whom was the mark, showing God's protection over the faithful.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 9:8 shows the prophet's confidence that no destruction would come on Jerusalem.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 9:8, the prophet fears that all the residue of Israel will be destroyed by God's fury, showing his concern rather than confidence in safety.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 9:5 and 9:6 together teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God shows justice by punishing the wicked without pity but shows mercy by marking the faithful for protection
God punishes everyone equally without distinction
God only spares the innocent children and punishes adults
God does not intervene in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God shows justice by punishing the wicked without pity but shows mercy by marking the faithful for protection
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together demonstrate that while God’s judgment is severe and without pity for the wicked, mercy is shown by marking certain individuals to be spared, highlighting both justice and mercy.

questions.question: What practical Christian lesson can be drawn from Ezekiel 9:8 regarding prayer in times of judgment?
options: It teaches believers to intercede in prayer and cry out to God even when facing overwhelming judgment
It suggests that prayer is useless in times of judgment
It instructs to ignore judgment and focus on personal gain
It encourages abandoning faith during difficult times
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches believers to intercede in prayer and cry out to God even when facing overwhelming judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:8 shows the prophet falling on his face and crying to God, illustrating the importance of prayer and intercession amidst calamity, a model for believers to trust and petition God in hard times.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 9:7 and 9:6, what happens if the command to begin at the sanctuary is obeyed?
options: The house is defiled and the courts are filled with slain, showing judgment starts with those closest to God
The sanctuary is cleansed and the city is saved
The people repent immediately and the slaying stops
The sanctuary remains untouched and peaceful
questions.correctAnswer: The house is defiled and the courts are filled with slain, showing judgment starts with those closest to God
questions.explanation: Obedience to the command in verse 6 leads to the fulfillment in verse 7 where the sanctuary is defiled and the courts filled with slain, emphasizing that judgment begins at the Lord’s house and with its leaders.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 9:9 reveal about the attitude of the people towards God, and how does this relate to the judgment described?
options: They claim the Lord has forsaken the earth and does not see, justifying God's judgment
They praise God and repent for their sins
They ignore God but expect His blessings
They worship idols and reject all gods
questions.correctAnswer: They claim the Lord has forsaken the earth and does not see, justifying God's judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains that the people’s rebellious attitude, asserting God has forsaken the earth, contributes to their guilt and the resulting judgment, showing the consequences of rejecting God’s sovereignty.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 9:9, what reason is given for God's judgment on Israel and Judah?
options: The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great
They worshipped foreign gods openly
They built altars to Baal in the city
They neglected the temple sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 states that the iniquity of Israel and Judah is exceeding great, and this is the cause of God's judgment.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the land is full of blood, and the city full of perverseness' in Ezekiel 9:9 imply about the state of Jerusalem?
options: It was marked by violence and moral corruption
It was surrounded by enemies
It was prosperous and peaceful
It was abandoned and desolate
questions.correctAnswer: It was marked by violence and moral corruption
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 describes the land as full of blood and the city full of perverseness, indicating widespread violence and moral corruption.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 9:10, what does God declare about His attitude toward the people’s sins?
options: His eye shall not spare, neither will He have pity
He will forgive them if they repent
He will send prophets to warn them
He will exile them but restore them later
questions.correctAnswer: His eye shall not spare, neither will He have pity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:10 explicitly states that God will not spare or have pity, but will recompense their way upon their head.

questions.question: Who reported back to God after carrying out the command in Ezekiel 9:11?
options: The man clothed with linen who had the inkhorn by his side
The six men with slaughter weapons
Ezekiel himself
The cherubim
questions.correctAnswer: The man clothed with linen who had the inkhorn by his side
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:11 records that the man clothed with linen, who had the inkhorn by his side, reported he had done as commanded.

questions.question: What command did God give to the man clothed with linen in Ezekiel 9:4?
options: To set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations
To smite all the people in the city
To gather the elders of Jerusalem
To build an altar in the city
questions.correctAnswer: To set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:4 describes God commanding the man clothed with linen to mark the foreheads of those lamenting over the abominations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 9:6, upon whom were the men instructed NOT to come near during the judgment?
options: Any man upon whom is the mark
The priests in the temple
The prophets in the city
The elders of the city
questions.correctAnswer: Any man upon whom is the mark
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 commands the executioners not to come near anyone who has the mark on their forehead.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 9 to emphasize the contrast between judgment and mercy?
options: Inclusio framing the narrative with the man clothed in linen
Simile comparing Jerusalem to a lion
Chiasm highlighting the order of events
Allegory illustrating spiritual blindness
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the narrative with the man clothed in linen
questions.explanation: The man clothed in linen appears at the beginning and end of the chapter (Ezekiel 9:2 and 9:11), creating an inclusio that frames the judgment narrative.

questions.question: The phrase 'go ye after him through the city, and smite' in Ezekiel 9:5 can be understood as a foreshadowing of what New Testament event?
options: The coming judgment at the end of days
The ministry of Jesus healing the sick
The Pentecost outpouring of the Holy Spirit
The resurrection of the dead
questions.correctAnswer: The coming judgment at the end of days
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:5’s command to execute judgment foreshadows the eschatological judgment described in the New Testament, such as in Revelation.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'mark' set upon the foreheads in Ezekiel 9:4, when compared to the marking in Revelation 7:3?
options: Both signify protection from divine judgment
Both indicate those chosen for exile
Both symbolize sin and guilt
Both represent a covenant of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Both signify protection from divine judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:4 and Revelation 7:3 both describe a mark placed on the foreheads of the faithful to protect them from coming judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 9:8 records Ezekiel's plea to God to stop destroying the residue of Israel during the judgment.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:8 shows the prophet falling on his face and crying out to God, asking if He will destroy the remaining Israelites, confirming the statement.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'The LORD hath forsaken the earth, and the LORD seeth not' in Ezekiel 9:9 represents a genuine belief by the people of Jerusalem.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 quotes the people’s claim, but it is a false assumption as God declares He sees and judges their iniquity.

questions.question: What is the original Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'mark' (often rendered as 'tav') in Ezekiel 9:4?
options: A sign or token indicating ownership or protection
A curse or punishment
A written law or commandment
A place of worship
questions.correctAnswer: A sign or token indicating ownership or protection
questions.explanation: The Hebrew letter 'tav' (ת) in Ezekiel 9:4 was used as a mark or sign, often indicating ownership or protection from harm.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 9:7, God commands the defilement of the house and filling the courts with the slain. This act symbolizes what broader theological theme?
options: The purification of the temple through judgment
The restoration of the temple for the exiles
The building of a new sanctuary
The eternal blessing of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The purification of the temple through judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:7’s defilement by the slain symbolizes God's purging of sin from His sanctuary, a theme of purification by judgment.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of marking the faithful for protection from judgment, similar to Ezekiel 9?
options: Exodus 12:7, 13 (Passover blood on doorposts)
Genesis 12:1 (Call of Abraham)
Leviticus 16 (Day of Atonement)
Numbers 13 (Spies sent into Canaan)
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 12:7, 13 (Passover blood on doorposts)
questions.explanation: The Passover in Exodus required marking doorposts with blood to protect the household from death, paralleling the protective mark in Ezekiel 9.

questions.question: How does the judgment scene in Ezekiel 9 relate to the concept of divine justice in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: It reflects the belief that the gods punish moral corruption decisively
It depicts a unique Israelite practice without parallels
It emphasizes mercy over justice unlike other cultures
It shows indifference to societal sins
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the belief that the gods punish moral corruption decisively
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, divine justice often involved severe punishment for moral corruption, as Ezekiel 9 shows with God's decisive judgment.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the specific instruction given to the man clothed with linen regarding the people in Jerusalem?
options: To mark the foreheads of those who mourn the city's abominations
To slay all inhabitants without mercy
To gather a census of the city
To cleanse the temple of idols
questions.correctAnswer: To mark the foreheads of those who mourn the city's abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:4 commands the man clothed with linen to go through Jerusalem and set a mark upon the foreheads of those who sigh and cry for the abominations done in the city, indicating God's distinction between the righteous and the wicked.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily demonstrated by His command to utterly slay old and young but spare those with the mark?
options: Justice
Omnipotence
Mercy
Omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 shows God's justice in punishing sin without partiality while sparing those who are marked, illustrating divine righteousness and judgment.

questions.question: In the vision, what is the significance of the man clothed with linen having a writer's inkhorn by his side?
options: He is to record the names of the faithful
He is the executor of judgment
He is a priest offering sacrifices
He is a prophet delivering a message
questions.correctAnswer: He is to record the names of the faithful
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 and 9:11 describe the man clothed with linen with a writing inkhorn, symbolizing his role in marking those who are to be spared, indicating the divine prerogative to distinguish the faithful from the wicked.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 9:3 reflect the holiness of God in relation to His presence in the temple?
options: God's glory departs from the cherub to the threshold
God descends to dwell among the people
God's presence intensifies over the altar
God hides His glory within the temple
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory departs from the cherub to the threshold
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:3 reveals God's holiness as His glory moves away from the inner sanctuary, signifying judgment and departure due to the people's sin, highlighting divine purity and separation from wickedness (cf. Exodus 33:20).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Ezekiel 9:5-6 and Ezekiel 9:10 teach about God's response to sin?
options: God executes impartial judgment without pity on unrepentant sin
God delays judgment to show mercy to all
God punishes only the leaders and spares the common people
God uses human agents to forgive sins
questions.correctAnswer: God executes impartial judgment without pity on unrepentant sin
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 command the execution of judgment without sparing anyone except those marked, and verse 10 confirms God will not have pity but recompense upon their heads, showing God's righteous and impartial justice.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 9:9 emphasize the spiritual condition of Jerusalem and its people?
options: The land is full of blood and the city full of perverseness
The people are repentant and seek God
The city is prosperous and free of sin
The land is barren but the people are faithful
questions.correctAnswer: The land is full of blood and the city full of perverseness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 declares the extreme sinfulness of Israel and Judah, highlighting the pervasiveness of violence and moral corruption, underscoring the necessity of divine judgment.

questions.question: What does the command in Ezekiel 9:7 to 'defile the house' by filling the courts with the slain signify about God's judgment?
options: The temple itself is judged and defiled by the people's sins
The temple is to be purified by sacrifice
God will protect the temple from all harm
The priests will be spared from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The temple itself is judged and defiled by the people's sins
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:7 implies that because of the people's sins, even the sanctuary is defiled by judgment, illustrating God's intolerance of sin within His holy dwelling.

questions.question: What does the response of Ezekiel in Ezekiel 9:8 teach about the prophet's role in intercession and lamentation?
options: He falls on his face and pleads for mercy
He celebrates the justice of God
He commands the execution to continue
He remains silent in the vision
questions.correctAnswer: He falls on his face and pleads for mercy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:8 shows the prophet's compassionate intercession, expressing grief over the destruction of Israel, reflecting the prophetic role as mediator and mourner.

questions.question: Considering Ezekiel 9:1 and Ezekiel 9:2, what does the presence of six men with slaughter weapons and one man clothed in linen symbolize in the divine judgment scene?
options: The executioners of God's judgment and the divine recorder
The priests and the Levites of the temple
The kings and their warriors
The angels of mercy and peace
questions.correctAnswer: The executioners of God's judgment and the divine recorder
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:1-2 describes six men equipped for destruction representing God's agents of judgment, and one clothed in linen with an inkhorn symbolizing the one who records or marks the righteous, highlighting God's sovereign control over judgment.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the marking of certain individuals in Ezekiel 9:4 and the command to spare them in 9:6?
options: Divine election and preservation of the faithful
Universal salvation of all inhabitants
Human ability to save themselves
Annihilation of the wicked without distinction
questions.correctAnswer: Divine election and preservation of the faithful
questions.explanation: The marking of those who mourn sin (Ezekiel 9:4) and sparing them from death (9:6) reveals God's sovereign choice to preserve a remnant, consistent with the doctrine of election.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 9:11 demonstrate the faithfulness of God's servants in executing divine commands?
options: The man clothed with linen reports he has done as commanded
The servants refuse to carry out the harsh judgment
The man clothed with linen questions the judgment
The servants show mercy to all
questions.correctAnswer: The man clothed with linen reports he has done as commanded
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:11 shows obedience and faithfulness of God's servant who fulfills the instructions exactly, indicating trustworthiness in carrying out divine judgment.

questions.question: What sceptic's claim does Ezekiel 9:9-10 address regarding God's awareness and justice?
options: Sceptics claim God has forsaken the earth and does not see evil; the passage teaches God sees all and will recompense iniquity
Sceptics claim God is indifferent to sin; the passage teaches God ignores sin
Sceptics claim God is weak; the passage teaches God cannot punish
Sceptics claim God rewards sin; the passage teaches God blesses the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Sceptics claim God has forsaken the earth and does not see evil; the passage teaches God sees all and will recompense iniquity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9-10 confronts the false notion that God is absent or indifferent, affirming His omniscience and just recompense, countering sceptical objections.

questions.question: What aspect of God's holiness is revealed by His departure from the cherub to the threshold of the house in Ezekiel 9:3?
options: God cannot tolerate sin in His holy presence
God is indifferent to human sin
God is present everywhere regardless of sin
God approves of the people's actions
questions.correctAnswer: God cannot tolerate sin in His holy presence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:3 indicates that God's glory departs from its place due to the people's sins, emphasizing the inviolable holiness of God and His separation from sin.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Ezekiel 9 contribute to the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It illustrates God's righteous judgment and preservation of a faithful remnant
It depicts universal salvation without judgment
It introduces the New Covenant explicitly
It shows the final defeat of Satan
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's righteous judgment and preservation of a faithful remnant
questions.explanation: The chapter's depiction of judgment alongside marking the faithful fits the biblical theme of God purging sin while preserving a remnant for redemption, integral to redemptive history (cf. Romans 11:5).

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by God's instruction to begin judgment at His sanctuary in Ezekiel 9:6?
options: The holiness of God's house and the accountability of His people
The irrelevance of the temple in judgment
The temple as a place of refuge from judgment
The temple as a symbol of universal peace
questions.correctAnswer: The holiness of God's house and the accountability of His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 shows that judgment begins at the sanctuary, underscoring that those closest to God must be held to higher accountability because of the temple's sanctity.
